clue.text: Tight as a snake

definitions.meaning: slang for drunk, too far gone to stand up
a snake has no limbs at all, so it fits this description literally

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: British slang for very drunk, and literally lacking limbs like a serpent.

clue.text: Banking the Milanese way?

parts.note: Milan is the capital of Lombardy, and a London thoroughfare named after Lombard bankers has long been the heart of British banking; 'way' doubles as a road

explanation.surface: A question about how bankers in Milan do business.
explanation.walkthrough: Medieval moneylenders from Lombardy, the region round Milan, settled in one City of London street, which became shorthand for the British banking world.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London street long synonymous with banking takes its name from Lombard moneylenders from the Milan region.

clue.text: Engage as King George with pupil

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
the pupil of the eye is called its apple

explanation.surface: A monarch called George takes on a schoolchild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' looks like a schoolchild, but it is the eye's pupil, traditionally the 'apple' of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with an opponent or problem is to engage with it closely.

clue.text: English king went in for red wine

indicators.note: the king's name has gone inside the words red wine, so his letters sit among theirs

explanation.surface: An English monarch goes out of his way to get some claret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went in for' reads as 'chose' but signals that the name is tucked inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin was an Anglo-Saxon king of Northumbria in the seventh century.

clue.text: Breathing space for organisation of replicas

indicators.note: organising the letters of the word means arranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranging copies to leave some room to breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing space' sounds like a pause; here it is literal, an opening insects and whales breathe through.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiracle is a breathing hole, such as the pores on an insect's body or a whale's blowhole.

clue.text: Return of limitation in money for high church job

indicators.note: the turned limitation sits inside the word for money

parts.note: pay is money earned

indicators.note: a return sends the word for limitation back the way it came

parts.note: a cap is a limit, as in a spending cap

explanation.surface: A salary cap reversed to fund a senior clergy post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns the word for limitation backwards before 'in' places it inside the word for money; 'high church job' is the Pope's office, not a High Church parish.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office of Pope, the highest position in the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Take the moral high ground-take in fruit

indicators.note: the letter for take goes inside the fruit

parts.note: a peach is a fruit
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone sanctimonious grabbing some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: R (take, from the Latin 'recipe' on prescriptions) goes inside PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to lecture others moralistically, adopting a superior moral stance.

clue.text: Nonstop trouble with Peter amid the like with Paul

indicators.note: trouble stirs the two apostles' names together and jumbles their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Two apostles, Peter and Paul, constantly squabbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' scrambles the letters of PETER and PAUL together; 'with' and 'amid the like with' only link the two names in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetual means everlasting or continuous, never ceasing.

clue.text: Limit with penalty

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for with, as in con brio
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: A restriction that comes with a fine attached.
explanation.walkthrough: CON means 'with' in Italian or Spanish, familiar from musical directions like con brio.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to restrict or keep within bounds.

clue.text: For the moment we hail men wandering…

indicators.note: letters that wander move about into another order

explanation.surface: We greet men who are roaming about, for now.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots lead into the next clue, completing the film cliché 'Meanwhile, back at the ranch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means in the interim, during the time being.

clue.text: . (back at the) station managed by companion

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a sheep station run by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue finishes the old film line 'Meanwhile, back at the ranch'. In Australia a large sheep or cattle farm is called a station.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and New Zealand a station is a large farm, much like an American cattle spread.

clue.text: Lots of minutes, without number, a lot of them from university

indicators.note: here meaning outside: the word for lots of minutes goes around the number

parts.note: each hour is sixty minutes, so several hours are lots of minutes
a degree of arc is divided into sixty minutes, so one degree is a lot of minutes

explanation.surface: A tangled sentence about time and quantity, ending at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense 'outside'. 'Them' points back to minutes: one angular degree holds sixty minutes of arc.
explanation.definitionFit: An honours degree is a bachelor's qualification awarded by a university at a higher standard than a pass.

clue.text: Trembler like writer

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: Someone nervous, much like an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trembler' suggests a nervous person; it is the tree whose leaves quiver in the slightest breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The trembling aspen is a poplar whose leaves shake in the wind.

clue.text: Extra performance taking in anti-racist body

indicators.note: the word for performance takes the body's initials inside it

parts.note: action means performance or deeds
CRE was the Commission for Racial Equality, a former British body

explanation.surface: An additional show that admits an equality campaign group.
explanation.walkthrough: The CRE, Britain's Commission for Racial Equality, merged into a wider commission in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: An accretion is something added on, a gradual growth by extra layers.

clue.text: Voting on performance for change of calling?

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after the other piece

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Casting votes about a show, for a career change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like a vocation, but it means what you are called: a deed poll is the legal document for changing your name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is the British legal deed by which someone formally changes their name.

clue.text: Arthur's father to wait, minimally dressed?

parts.note: to pend is to remain undecided or wait
wearing only a rag, one has a rag on

explanation.surface: King Arthur's father waiting around in scanty clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Arthurian legend King Arthur's father is Uther, whose title is the one sought here.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther, the father of King Arthur in legend, bore the title meaning chief dragon.

clue.text: Old town in dandy office

indicators.note: the ancient city goes inside the word for dandy

parts.note: a beau is a fashionable man or dandy
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: An ancient settlement inside a fop's workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: UR, the ancient city in Mesopotamia, is the crossword's standard old town.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or agency, and also a writing desk.

clue.text: Cat with alternative line coming soon

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
or introduces an alternative
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A cat with another line, a trailer for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming soon' reads like a cinema trailer slogan, but stands for the day after today.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomorrow is the day ahead, the near future that will arrive shortly.

clue.text: Gift of explosive containing beer

indicators.note: the explosive holds the beer within its letters

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, an explosive
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A present of dynamite with a pint inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gift' looks like a present, but it means a natural ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural ability or aptitude.

clue.text: Variety of thistle from the Baltic

indicators.note: a variety of the word is another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A type of thistle native to the Baltic region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' sounds botanical, a type of plant, but signals the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettish is an older name for Latvian, the language and people of a Baltic state.

clue.text: Posh talk of such as no.2in the table

parts.note: noble means aristocratic, upper-class
gas means idle chatter

explanation.surface: Upper-class chatter about something at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The table' is not dining furniture but the periodic table, where element number 2 is helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, element 2 of the periodic table, is one of the inert gases in its final column.

clue.text: Roads in winter may be like teeth under protest

definitions.meaning: icy roads are spread with grit for traction
clenched teeth when enduring something unwillingly

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: icy streets get spread with grit, and someone enduring something reluctantly clenches their jaw.

clue.text: Make it possible to take in some elements

indicators.note: the word for take goes inside the chosen letters
only some of the letters of the word elements are used, its first three

parts.note: to nab is to take or seize

explanation.surface: Allowing one to absorb some chemical elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some elements' means part of the word itself: ELE, its first three letters, with NAB put 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to make something possible or allow it.

clue.text: Form part of intestinal cut, not otherwise

indicators.note: cutting the word loses its last letter

parts.note: enteric means relating to the intestines

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of the word not are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon's note about intestinal surgery done properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' drops the final C of ENTERIC, and 'otherwise' rearranges NOT into NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter into an arrangement is to become a party to it, to take part in it.

clue.text: See 26
Last word for something straight before turn

indicators.note: the straight thing comes ahead of the turn

parts.note: proverbially something is straight as a die
a U is a turn, as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: Final remarks on going straight before a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'straight as a die' makes a die the something straight; a U-turn supplies U.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, the final thing said on parting.

clue.text: See 26
Advocate of exchange including large element of risk

indicators.note: the word for exchange takes the chosen letters inside it

parts.note: to barter is to exchange goods

indicators.note: a large element of the word means most of its letters, all but the last

explanation.surface: A champion of trade who brings in a hefty dose of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large element of risk' takes all of that word except its final letter; 'including' puts it inside the word for exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who pleads in the higher courts, an advocate.

clue.text: Child of the new age in Cuban form? I wish!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Child of the new age in Cuban form? I wish!': 'I wish!' defines the phrase, but no parse of the rest builds it and searches found no fuller text or blog
annotationWithheld.clue: Child of the new age in Cuban form? I wish!
